entries.text: Rock Fall: A loud rumbling is heard. The characters must make a Dexterity + Alert / Evasion check to avoid being Damaged by a perilous rock fall or split up.
Living Stone: Characters encounter a large rocky obstruction, blocking their way forwards. It turns out to be a sleeping Graveler, who is not entirely happy with being woken up.
Colony of Glimmora: The party find the floor covered in spiky (Toxic) debris and the strange rocky flower-like creatures, clinging to the cavern walls that made it.
Carvings: Carved in the cavern walls are multiple strange depictions of ancient Pokémon and humans. The players are perhaps able to glean some insight into them with a Clever + Lore check.
Gemstone Cave: Beautiful crystalline gemstones glitter. Sableye can be seen feasting on them. Perhaps the characters find an evolution stone, a Carbink or other precious mineral amongst them.
Unfathomable Chasm: A huge abyss lays in the characters path. A group skill check, or clever use of Pokémon is required to cross or descend it. An unsuccessful check adds time to their journey.
Bioluminescent Mushrooms: The party encounter clouds of strange glowing (hallucinogenic) spores, created by Morelull and Shiinotic.
Blood Suckers: Light from the characters torches or Pokémon disturbs a large nesting ground of Golbat, who then attempt to feed from them.
Odd Echoes: Echoes mimic the character’s and their Pokémon’s voices... Then begin saying things they haven’t said.

Archeologist: The group encounter a lone, slightly crazy archaeologist who insists that there are fossils or ruins nearby. They attempt to get the party to help them find them. Perhaps the fossils (if found) are possessed by Specrelec however...
Pickpocket: A thief bumps into and steals something important from one of the characters. Perhaps the thief is a human or a group of the elemental monkey Pokémon.

Piss Off: One of the character’s Pokémon encounters a mean and battle scarred old Persian, who claims to be called “Piss Off” (as that’s what people call him). He attempts to get the character’s Pokémon to leave them or cause some other form of trouble for the party.
Strange Ooze: The characters see a strange slimy substance oozing out of a sewer grate. If they ask around food has been going missing and people getting sick. The culprit is Chimaooze.
Strange Salesman: A strange merchant accosts the players, and tries to sell them rare and exotic “souvenirs” or cheap potions. Something about them seems off though.
Shakedown: A group of thugs attempt to shake down the characters or a nearby NPC down for valuables, information or something else.
The Challenger: Hearing of one of the characters’ exploits. They’re approached and challenged to a battle. Perhaps to test their skill before asking for help, or just for the honor of defeating them.
Street Performance: A crowd has gathered, watching a mysterious and elegant street performer and their Pokémon assistant, at the finale of their act. They suddenly vanish however.
Mad Prophet: The characters encounter someone, prophesying imminent doom. None of the locals seem to pay them any attention however.
Mystery Poke Ball: The characters find a lost or discarded Poke Ball, they are unable to open it, but it does seem to contain something.
Lost Pokémon: The characters encounter a lost Pokémon, it is dejectedly looking for its Trainer. If they help it, they are handsomely rewarded by its rich Trainer.
Kleptomaniac: The party are followed by a Klefki (or Johtonian Klefki) who wishes to add their trinkets, keys or sharp objects to its collection.
Graffiti Artist: The party are (wrongly) accused of defacing Trait as Smeargle runs away...
Hungry Cacti: The characters are stalked through the dunes at night by sinister moving cacti. Encounter with aggressive group of Cacturne.
Abandoned Caravanserai: The characters stumble upon an abandoned building, half filled with sand. There could still be some useful supplies within or a nearby water source...
Sandstorm: A harsh sandstorm kicks up, caused by Dusteon or Claydoll. Perhaps it is trying to herd them out of danger. Regardless they must find or make shelter.
Mirage: A beautiful oasis can be seen in the distance. But upon reaching it, or making a successful Insight + Nature check, it vanishes. A single, hardy berry bush is all that they find.
Unquenchable Thirst: A lone and bedraggled person or Pokémon is found dying of dehydration. They keep asking for more water and drinking any that the characters offer them.
Sand Shark: A fin like protrusion can be seen, as the sand Moves below the characters feet. They are suddenly attacked by an Alpha Garchomp or (Orrean) Sharpedo.
Trade Caravan: A Camerupt mounted group of merchants makes their way slowly towards the players. They hastily make camp and offer, food, water and other goods at exorbitant prices.

Trapinch Trap: The characters are ambushed by a horde of Trapinch who spit sand at them and try to drag them or their supplies below the sand and into their nest. The basin-like area rapidly turns into treacherous quicksand.

Hopelessly Lost: The characters realize they have been going in circles for some time. Adds a significant amount of travel time and requires an Insight + Nature check to find the correct route. Mandibuzz or Rexquiem circle hungrily, watching from from above...

Fossilized Find: A wind and sand scoured rock face or riverbed reveals fossilized Pokémon Skeletons within. On a successful Dexterity / Clever + Nature / Crafts check the characters are able to safely remove 1 or 2.

Avalanche: A large Avalugg or Gigalanche has awoken from a long slumber and started moving. This causes an avalanche to begin crashing down the slopes towards the party, requiring quick thinking and use of Pokémon or a Dexterity + Evasion check to avoid it.

Injured Hiker: The party encounter a hiker or pilgrim who has been injured in a rockfall or (inadvertently) by a wild Onix. They require help getting to safety or at least out of the elements, warm and dry. The hiker rewards the characters for their aid.
The Luchadore: A wild Hawlucha is seeking to make itself stronger in order to beat a rival. It challenges one of the characters to a battle in order to improve its abilities.
Slipping Scree: Rocks slide out from under some of the characters feet, they go sliding over the edge of a precipice! The others and their Pokémon must act fast to rescue them.

Thundering Dragon: Thunder suddenly echoes, and lightning streaks across the sky, as heavy rain begins to pour. Unovan Altaria is grieving the (supposed) death of its chicks and using its powers in rage.
Rickety Bridge: The party must cross a large crevasse. A rickety looking rope suspension bridge seems like the only way to progress...

Cliff Rookery: The party encounter a cliff overhang, holding the nesting ground of Rookidee and Corvisquire, watched over by an old pair of Corviknight. The Pokémon are wary of the characters but unaggressive.

Gogoat Shepherd: The characters encounter a boy and his Herdier, herding Gogoat and Skiddoo. Some have gone missing however and he suspects a strong wild Pokémon to be at blame... He and his mother offer the party a place to rest and a meal should they help him find them or capture the Pokémon responsible.
Gigalith’s Eruption: Orrean Gigalith is fighting for territory with a strong opponent. This has the unfortunate effect of molten rocks being shot everywhere however, threatening a nearby village.

Monastic Mess: The party hear a loud bell chime (coming from Bronzong) echo through the valleys and crags. Eventually seeing an isolated monastery higher up the mountain. The monks found within are friendly and offer the players a place to rest. The bell marked the beginning of a celebration where the next leader of their order is chosen (possibly to ...interesting results).
Sickness: A character or their Pokémon becomes sick, entering a rapidly declining state. The illness is a mystery, the others must try to help them or find someone who can.
Contamination: Food and water supplies are mysteriously contaminated and ruined. Perhaps inadvertently by a stowaway Poison-Type Pokémon. Perhaps requiring them to fish or dive for food.

Navigational Failure: Navigation devices fail due to interference of some kind. An Insight + Nature check must be made to read stars etc, a failure may result in extended travelling time, the group becoming lost or some other negative occurrence.
Wailord Pod: The characters encounter a pod of Wailord, who are currently in mating season and do not appreciate the party’s presence in their midst.
Strange Lights: Lanturn are hunting near the party. This may have the effect of a character or Pokémon falling overboard while distracted by their enticing lights.
Becalmed: The seas are becalmed, the characters must make use of their Pokémon creatively, or days are added to the journey, supplies used etc.
Weird Weather: A lone Castform is trailing the group at a distance and creating strange Weather phenomena. It’s reasons for doing so are unclear, Is it attempting to harm or help them?
Naval Encounter: The group are attacked by pirates or another type of enemy vessel. Perhaps they mean to rob them or just delay their progress for some other reason.
Drifting Survivor: An unconscious shipwreck survivor is found afloat. When roused they tell of a powerful Pokémon or ship that attacked them and their companions.

Travelling Merchant: The group encounters a friendly mercantile vessel, or trader riding a Lapras, they hail the group and offer their goods. Use Travelling Merchant table or roll once on the Large Market table for available wares.
Stormy Seas: A storm is brewing on the horizon. The party must make a Clever + Etiquette / Tough + Athletics check to navigate the dangerous waters and massive waves safely.
Odd Wreckage: The characters encounter floating debris from a destroyed vessel or lost cargo, the Storyteller decides on, or rolls for item(s) the characters find.
Stampede: A large herd of Bouffalant or Rhyhorn rush towards the characters. Dexterity + Evasion checks, a group Tough + Intimidate check or quick thinking is required to not get trampled.

Brushfire Break: In the distance the party can see smoke billowing from the dry brush, wild Pokémon go fleeing, followed by flames rapidly spreading out from the area. A Fire-Type Pokémon or some other source has started a brushfire. Quick thinking is required to halt the fire’s spread.

Electrical Discharge: The characters notice a weird static surrounding them, and they get small shocks from any metal gear they’re carrying. (Zebstrika and Heliolisk are fighting over a heavily laden berry bush nearby).
The Lone Rider: A lone rider swoops in from the distance, atop their Staraptor. They warn the party of dangerous poachers operating in the area, but also mention the bounty on their heads.
Waterhole: The characters find a large watering hole, being used by many different Pokémon. The wild Pokémon seem wary of each other and the party but not actively aggressive currently.

Anthill attack: A huge Durant Nest is under siege by a group of Heatmor. Durengine and Heatmega battle it out on top of hill. If the character’s pick a side to help and come out victorious, they are rewarded in berries or some form of useful items, found by their side.

Wounded Pride: The party encounters a wounded Luxio or Litleo (possibly hurt by poachers). It seems young and likely has also been separated from its pride. It’s very distrustful of the characters and may lash out at them if they attempt to help it.

Roadside Assistants: The characters encounter a broken down vehicle, with two students attempting to fix it (badly). They are apparently on their way to join their professor on his next research expedition. If the characters manage to repair their vehicle or offer them a lift, they’re rewarded with a Held Item, evolutionary stone or some Poke Balls.
Nomadic Aritst: The party find a wandering artist in a remote locale. They’re feeling uninspired apparently. But a battle may just fix that. (They have a strong team with Streagle as their Advanced).

Apricorn Grove: The party find a grove of Apricorn trees. If they attempt to pick them, they’re scolded by an old woman who claims they’re hers. If the party sincerely apologize she offers to make them a ball or two each however.
Suspicious Sandcastle: On the beach the group encounter a huge and elaborate sandcastle... Small footprints can be seen leading towards it, but not away from it. (Palosand Encounter).
Merciless Mereanie: In the shallows, Corsola can be seen attempting to flee from Mereanie. Corsola does not look to be in a good state and is suffering from the Badly Poisoned Status...

Dance Battle: The characters encounter a group of Ludicolo who seem up for a challenge. Though not of the usual kind... The Ludicolo want a dance off! Beauty / Cool + Perform / Charm checks are required to win here. Bonus points if the group have Pokémon with “Dance” Moves.
Hungry Cramorant: The party spot a Large Cramorant attempting to swallow a whole Snubull. They can see Snubull has a bow tied around its neck...
Crab Rave: The party encounter hundreds of small, newly hatched Crabrawler or Cracolite causing havoc on the shoreline...

Fishing Contest: A fishing contest is underway. The party are able to enter. Most caught and biggest caught are the two categories. A man named Bob is selling fishing rods and Lure Balls nearby. Prizes are a Water Stone and a the Biggest Catch Trophy (Same effect as Amulet Coin).

Coastal Cave: The party find a mysterious semi-submerged cave. Heading inside they find crystalline growths. The water-type variants of Ralts and Hatenna can be seen cautiously watching the party. If they attempt to catch one, they may end up in a battle with protective Alpha Gallade and Hatterene.
Cheeky Wingull: While having something to eat, the party are swarmed by Wingull. The Wingull attempt to get them to drop their food by dive bombing and defecating on them...

Lake Serpent: One of the party members or their Pokémon spots a long shadow moving beneath the water’s surface. An Insight + Alert check leads them to discovering the shadow belongs to (Orrean) Milotic. It may take some clever thinking to capture it should they want to.

Tubing Race: The party encounter a race being set up. Trainers are towed on circular inflatables behind water-types, they may borrow a viable Pokémon if they don’t have one. The prize is a Mega Stone. (The race is composed of various skill challenges and obstacles).

Restless Spirit: The party encounter an open grave or a rotting gibbet with a crumbling skeleton hanging from it. A Yamask appears, wailing and moaning pitifully. A successful Insight + Nature or Clever + Lore check infers that the grave or skeleton has been recently disturbed. Finding a missing bone or burial item and returning it quiets Yamask’s sorrow.
Wandering Wisps: Flickering wisps attempt to lead the party somewhere. Roll 1D4 on a 1-2 they lead the group to an encounter with Alpha Dusknoir on a 3-4 they lead them to a useful Held Item.
The Voices: A character begins hearing voices whispering to them and influencing them to kill the rest of the party. Have them roll current Will. If they get under 4 they become Charmed...
Unnatural Darkness: Thick fog rolls in and the skies darken strangely, becoming suddenly starless or so overcast it appears to be night. Midnight Weather is in effect for future encounters.

The One: The party encounter a dark haired, pale, emotionless woman. In an unearthly voice she points at one of the characters and proclaims. “You... you are the one.” She hands them a Soothe Bell or a Weapon. Then wordlessly leaves, her feet don’t seem to touch the ground.

Mysterious Merchants: The group encounter some brightly dressed and merry merchants. They happily break bread and offer their wares. Later, the party fall into a deep sleep. When they awake the merchants are gone, but their camp and wagon remains (now ancient and mostly destroyed).
Poltergeist: Nearby objects animate and begin flying at the party! Roll Poltergeist from Fauxeary or Golurk against all party members. The Pokémon appears afterwards and an encounter begins.

Possessed Pokémon: The character’s Pokémon begin to act strangely, getting worse over time. Acting skittishly or flinching away from their trainers and disobeying commands. Eventually attempting to flee, running to a nearby clearing and are found in a circle, motionless but conscious. They snap out of it and seem confused and sad when roused.
Creepy Doll: A member of the party finds a discarded doll, they feel oddly drawn to keep it. At a crucial moment during the adventure it awakens to aid them, becoming a Fauxeary or Voodoll.
Nightmare Realm: When resting, the party enter a strange nightmare realm where personalities are inverted. Nightmarach, (Unovan) Skiploom or Delta Hypno is behind it!

Ancient Barrows: The party find an ancient burial ground. Tunnels lead into the tombs. The They can see treasures laid out. If they disturb anything a horde battle begins against Shuppet, Haunter, (Johtonian) Tinkatink, Houndstone and Misdreavus. If they win, they find a Relic Gold.

The Countess: While travelling, the Weather turns and the party must seek shelter. They find a creepy looking château. A strange elderly butler opens the door and invites them in. The lady of the house is very charming, and treats them to dinner and offers them rooms for the night. But something seems very off about the whole affair. The windows on the upper floors are all barred and there are seemingly no other staff or residents, unusual for a place of that size...

Strong Winds: The winds suddenly pick up to a dangerous degree. Depending on method of transport, this may add travel time or blow the group off course. Strong Wind Weather is in effect for all other encounters.
Sky Racer: A young woman dives towards the group atop her Dragonite or Talonflame. She challenges the party to a race. (Prize money is won or deducted as if it was a battle).
Savage Skarmory: The group encounter a flock of Skarmory, who seem rather enraged at their presence. Unless the characters can calm them, battle ensues.
Mass Migration: Many Tailow and Swellow can be seen on their long migratory journey. One seems to be struggling however, falling behind and being pecked at by the others...

Drifting Drifloon: A large group of Drifloon float alongside the party. Attempting to “help” by grasping at bags and the characters themselves. A smaller party member or Pokémon may be carried off somewhere...
Thermal Columns: Fletchinder or Braviary can be seen soaring alongside the party in thermal currents. On a successful Insight + Nature check, Stamina Cost for travelling that day is reduced.
Millenium Comet: The party witness a comet passing by, they feel a sense of mystical wonder and a blue light momentarily envelopes them. Jirachi restores 3 of their Will Points.

Maiden Voyage: The group encounter a rather eccentric older gentleman and his two young companions flying in a hot air balloon. They’ve been somewhat blown of course and would like assistance. They reward the group with Air Balloons and some “vitals” each.

Cloud Sea: Breaching a layer of cloud, the party are met with a stunning sight. A whole ocean like ecosystem of Skyphozoa, Collosoar, Halofin, Seraphish, Iridesceel and Jourmarine, not to mention various types of bird-like Pokémon.

Lost Mail: Some mail must have slipped from a delivery, it can be seen being carried on the wind. If the players manage to snatch it from the air, it just so happens to have an address to a location nearby where they’re heading. Delivering it nets then a substantial reward, as it was a letter proclaiming the recipient to be the inheritor of a small fortune.

Asteroid Field: The ship enters a dense field of fast-moving debris. The ship / pilot must make 3 Dexterity + Evasion / Handling checks. For each failure, the Vehicle takes 4 Dice of Rock-Type Damage.
Space Pirates: An armed vessel demands ₽10000 or an item of similar value. If refused, Vehicle Combat begins. The pirates have a boarding teleporter.

Abandoned Research Station: The party encounter a deserted outpost, it’s crew fled due to an unknown threat. It seems their research was to do with viruses. If the party linger, they are attacked by UB-24 Virus.
Porygon Probe: The party detect a damaged scientific probe broadcasting its location. Recovering and returning it to its owners earns them ₽5000.
Solar Flares: A nearby star releases a burst of radiation. The ship’s sensors and communicators stop functioning, but can be repaired with a successful Clever + Technology check.
Customs Inspection: An official patrol vessel requests permission to board and inspect the party’s cargo. They become suspicious if refused.

Frozen Passenger: A small escape pod is drifting nearby. Its occupant is alive in suspended animation and carries identification showing where they need to be returned. If awoken, they suffer from Frostbite (3) Status and begin taking Lethal Damage.
Meltan Meteor: A mineral rich meteor is identified on the ship’s scanners. Unbeknownst to the party, however. The rock contains no mineral wealth, but the strange liquid metal Pokémon, Meltan.

Merchant Vessel: A travelling merchant offers general store goods, and four random items from the Arms and Augmentations Dealer at 10% above their usual prices. They also have 1 special weapon or piece of equipment for sale.
Ghost Station: The party encounter a small space station. Entirely crewed by Rotom Drones. It seems as though the place should have several human crew. All of who are conspicuously absent.

Dreadful Mire: Stinging acidic rain begins to fall and the filthy marsh water turns almost black as the party progresses further. Poisonous Wastes Field-Type and Acid Rain Weather are in effect for the next two encounters.
Dewpider’s Pool: The party encounter a small group of Dewpider excitedly skating across the water’s surface. An Insight + Nature check reveals some Revival Herbs growing on the bank.
Quicksand Quagmire: Some or all of the party find themselves rapidly sinking into the muddy bog. A Dexterity + Athletic check or quick thinking is required to escape the sucking mud.
Toxicroak’s Toll: Alpha Toxicroak blocks the party’s path. Croaking and puffing out its poison sack intimidatingly, it holds out a hand expectantly. It seems to be demanding some form of tribute...
Snapping Jaws: While crossing a rickety bridge, or wading through the water. The party are snapped at by Dreadmaw or (Alolan) Krockoroc. They might steal a pack or some food supplies.
Cruising Clodsire: Swimming slowly up a channel, Clodsire can be seen carrying a number of Wooper. The cheeky Wooper begin attempting to splash and muddy the party or their Pokémon.

Witch’s Hut: The party encounter a strange hut on a large mound. If they approach, the hut begins to rise, showing that is resting on a huge Torterra’s back. The hut’s occupants (a slightly bedraggled old woman, and her Voodoll) call out to the party. She may offer the party a ride slightly closer to their destination or a bargain... But should they anger her at all she puts “curses” on them.
Marsh Gas: The party begin to smell something strange... If they have any exposed flames, or use Electric-Type attacks etc, the gas ignites suddenly! (The gas may last for more encounters).

Bibarrel Dam: The party encounter a large dam, Bidoof and Bibarell can be seen industriously working on it. (They might realize it is blocking an often used waterway, or endangering a nearby settlement however).
Vicious Bully: The party encounters some smaller Pokémon being bullied by (Orrean) Hakamo-o. If the group attack attempt to battle Hakamo-o, it calls for its parent Kommo-o.

Botanical Blunder: The party encounter a botanist in a spot of trouble. While conducting research on a rare flower found in the area, they where attacked by Swarm Form Combee. They ask the party to Forage (rolling normally) for a specific herb that may ease the swelling. (Encounter with Swarm Form Combee).

Brigands: The characters stumble upon an isolated hideaway. The occupants turn out to wanted by local law enforcement for kidnapping, piracy, racketeering and numerous other crimes... (They have some considerable loot and a person they’re holding for ransom stashed in their hideout).
Canopy Raiders: A noisy troupe of Aipom, Passimian or the “elemental monkeys” swing down from the canopy, snatching food, trinkets and gear from the party!
Cocunut Crabs: The characters encounter a somewhat disturbing sight. Large skull-like crab Pokémon known as Cruskull and Crabramuerte climbing coconut trees near the beach...
Seviper vs Zangoose: The party encounter an epic battle between Seviper and Zangoose. Their ever present hatred for each other coming to a boiling point...
Spice Growers: The party encounter a farmer, their Scovillain and Capsiwisp. They’re strengthening the spice of the famous chillis they grow. They may need a hand harvesting them...
Strange Voice: The party hear a voice calling out. The voice begins saying some rather incriminating things however. The voice turns out to be Chatot, it may have witnessed something...

Tropius’ Garden: The party discover a clearing full of fruit bearing trees and berry bushes. Tropius can been grazing from them, and curiously watch the party. They become somewhat upset if the party take too much of their delicious fruit however.
Dawn and Dusk: The party encounter a strange occurrence at either dawn or dusk. An odd ritualistic dance performed by the Pokémon Lunatone and Solrock...
Jungle Queen: The characters encounter a strange sight, many smaller Pokémon offering tribute at the feet of a magisterial Tsareena. Her “guards” don’t take kindly to them showing any disrespect.
Wild Weather: The Weather suddenly begins to drastically worsen! For future encounters Hail Weather, Snowy Terrain, and the Frozen Field-Type are in effect.
Mightyena Sled: A merchant speeds across the ice on a sled towed by Mighteyena. They’re happy to trade with the party, but say they’re in a rush to get to their destination before nightfall...
Beartic’s Den: The party stumble on Cubchoo playing outside of a (ice)cave entrance. If they startle them or try to capture them, an angry Alpha Beartic comes rushing out to attack them.
Igloo: The party find an igloo, smoke is rising from the chimney. The old hermit currently dwelling within offers them jerky and hot tea. They may be persuaded to teach them something useful too.
Hunter x Hunted: The party can see (Alolan) Ninetails hunting (Ruskovan) Bunnelby. It’s furiously attempting to dig into a warren. But flees in surprise when it notices the party.

Naughty or Nice: Delibird flies overhead, with a cheerful “Deliiii” it drops a present from its sack. Roll 1D4 on a 1-2 the present explodes doing 2 Set Damage to everyone in the party, (unless they can Evade). On 3-4 it is full of berries or random Held Items.

Frozen Lake: The party come to a large frozen lake, the ice looks “solid enough” to cross. (Ruskovan) Surprised Wimpod scatter out from a jetty, apparently feasting on leftover bait from an ice fisher. Eiscue can be seen sliding across the ice in the distance.

The Yokai: The party meet a fellow traveller who tells them a tale about a woman who froze to death waiting for a lover who spurned her. They jokingly warn that her vengeful spirit still haunts the area. (Later the party encounter Alpha Froslass during a blizzard).

Ranger’s Respite: The characters stumble upon a small shack. Used by the local rangers or hunters when working in the area. The door is locked, but the key is found or lock able to be picked on a successful Insight + Alert or Dexterity + Crafts check. The place is dry, out of the elements and there is a small wood-fired stove, a stack of dry firewood and some dried or tinned goods within.

Aurora Courtship: The party encounter a Tungryph who seems to be courting a mate (ineffectively). Clever + Lore checks to remember what they’ve heard about the Pokémon, or Insight + Empathy / Etiquette to hatch a plan. They are rewarded with an Ice Stone or “Tutor Move” from Tungryph’s Move list.
Somnorific Spores: The party accidentally disturb a group of Shroomish or Parasect. Who shower them with huge cloud of sleep inducing spores in their panic...

Fake Tears: A Pokémon can be heard, sounding very upset. The players find a distraught baby Pokémon. Seemingly separated from its parent. In reality it leads them into an ambush and attempts to steal their food.

Mushroom Gatherer: A friendly greeting calls out, and the characters see a young woman with a basket full of mushrooms nearby. She offers to share the location of where she found them. A successful Insight + Nature / Alert check nets them a few Tiny or Big Mushrooms but unsuccessful checks turn out to be angry Amoongus.

Dancing Blossoms: The party encounter a tranquil glade, where the light breaks through the heavy canopy. Bellossom are dancing in a circle, but flee as soon as they notice the characters. Perhaps leaving behind an item or a watching Oddish that trips over.

Webbed Path: Massive webs cover the trees, and block the path. A successful Dexterity / Clever + Stealth / Crafts check manages to cut a path through silently, without attracting the swarm of Ariados or Spidream that call this place home.

Hollow Guardians: A deforested area with a large gnarled stump lies in the character’s path. It gives off an eerie aura. The large stump transforms into Trevenant with smaller ones into Phantump should the party linger.

Mysterious Shrine: The party find a small shrine next to a crystal clear, waterfall. The shrine appears to have been built to honor the “guardian of the forest”. Drinking from the creek removes 1 level of Exhaustion and grants 3 Stamina points.
Poachers: The party come across a group of Poachers attempting to steal away a rare Pokémon from its parent. Conflict likely ensues...

The Wild Hunt: Characters encounter an Alpha Sawsbuck (appropriate seasonal form), being chased through the forest by a mysterious hunting party and their Lycanrock, who are tracking it. The hunters are mounted on Galarian Rapidash, and give off a strange almost otherworldly vibe.

Forester’s Retreat: The characters find a small cabin, where an old forester and their Scyther live. They offer the party tea or something stronger, and want the characters help with something. Offering to cook them dinner and teach their Pokémon a Move as payment.
Dueling Beetles: The characters encounter Heracross and Pinsir engaged in a battle. They may decide team up if the characters try to break up their match however...
Forager’s Delight: This section of the forest has an abundance natural resources, easily found and gathered. Roll once on each Forage Table.
